Nantes (-1, 142:143) collapsed 33:27 at home to previously winless Vardar in Round 5, with coach Gregory Cojean citing ongoing one-on-one finishing struggles. Plock at home are the pick.
writeup.selection: Orlen Wisla Plock to win (money line, 1.64 / -156)

writeup.text: Aalborg Handbold to win at 1.71 (-141) is the selection for Wednesday night's Group C top-spot showdown at Stade Pierre de Coubertin in Paris (20:45 CET). Unbeaten Aalborg lead Group C on 9 points (4-1-0, 170:145, +25) after defeating RK Celje 34:30 in Round 5 while rotating their bench behind Thomas Arnoldsen (6/8) and Juri Knorr, and the Danish champions already beat Paris Saint-Germain in Round 1 at Aalborg. Second-placed PSG (3-1-1, 7 points, 182:157) let a four-goal half-time lead slip in Wednesday's 29:28 defeat at eliminated HC Zagreb despite Ferran Sole's 10/11 outing, struggling against Zagreb's second-half 5-1 defence. Back unbeaten Aalborg on the money line.

writeup.text: Take Sporting Clube de Portugal to win at 1.65 (-154) when they visit GOG at Arena Svendborg on Thursday evening (18:45 CET) with Group D carryover points at stake. Unbeaten group leaders Sporting (4-1-0, 9 points, 191:165, +26) boast the highest-scoring attack in the competition at 38.2 goals per game, paced on Thursday by Francisco Costa's personal Champions League record 14 goals from 16 shots alongside brother Martim Costa in a 42:40 win over Kristianstad, having already beaten GOG in Lisbon in Round 1. Second-placed GOG (3-1-1, 7 points, 178:172) needed a buzzer-beating Kevin Moller save to salvage a 33:33 draw at Szeged after surrendering a 6:0 late run. Sporting to win is the pick.

writeup.text: Back Dinamo Bucuresti to win at 1.70 (-143) in Thursday night's Group E finale at FDI Stadium in Montpellier (20:45 CET). Third-placed Dinamo (1-1-3, 3 points, 134:145) remain alive for the second Main Round berth after dismantling SAH - Aarhus 37:23 on Wednesday — the biggest Champions League victory in club history — led by Victor Iturizza (5/5), Haniel Langaro, and goalkeeper Ionut Iancu, and Dinamo also won the Round 1 meeting in Bucharest. Fourth-placed Montpellier (1-0-4, 2 points, 150:165) have lost four straight and are already eliminated following Thursday's 40:34 defeat at Barca, where centre back Pol Valera noted mounting player injuries and Benjamin Richert received a direct red card. Dinamo Bucuresti to win is our selection.
